desk.headline: Revenue up 15% to $45.5m, beat; loss of $1.29 per share, wider than expected; no guidance
results: Revenue rose 15% to $45.5m, helped by $3.1m more in league distributions and $2.6m more food, drink and merchandise sales on demand after the Knicks' NBA title.
Operating loss narrowed to $25.5m from $27.4m, as higher revenue outweighed $3.6m of Rangers spin-off costs.
Net loss widened to $31.1m ($1.29 per share) from $8.8m, mainly because $15.1m of other income a year ago swung to a $3.7m expense.
Results still include the Rangers business, which was spun off on 26 Oct 2026, after the quarter ended.
Cash fell to $40.0m from $164.5m at the end of June, while long-term debt rose to $282m from $242m.

guidance.summary: The company gave no financial guidance with these results.

watch: First quarter reported without the Rangers, giving a clean view of the Knicks-only business.
Ticket, sponsorship and merchandise demand during the title-defence season.
Cash and debt levels after the spin-off.
